haiku-low.q1: It returns the popular list with fallback: true and a reason. The model is not called.
haiku-low.q2: It keeps serving the previous rows until their as_of is 6 hours old, then falls back to the popular list.
haiku-low.q3: No. Candidate output goes only to the analytics store; the response builder has no reference to it. Shadow failures cause no user-visible change.
haiku-low.q4: Users whose SHA-256 of shadow_salt plus user_id, mod 10000, is below shadow_percent times 100. Only when shadow_version is set.
haiku-low.q5: A passing 7-day gate, ML lead approval matching the version and report hash, target loaded on at least 99% of pods, compatibility passing, and the expected revision still current.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED as decided. The plan leaves open whether a live A/B slice sits between shadow and the full switch.
haiku-low.q7: Pods poll the config service every 10 s, load the new version from the artifact store if missing, and switch. No redeploy.
haiku-low.q8: Shadow uses the same feature row the response used, carried in the queue event. Enqueue happens after the response, never blocks, and runs on a separate fleet.
haiku-low.q9: Events are dropped when the bounded queue is full. Workers discard events lagging over 60 s and count them. No user sees a change.
haiku-low.q10: One row per event in the analytics store holds both active and candidate items. A daily job compares them and stores a gate report in the registry.
haiku-low.q11: Compatibility is checked at registration, promotion, pod load, per active request, and per shadow event. Failing candidates are skipped, and activation is refused.
haiku-low.q12: One CAS config write sets active_version to previous_active and increments revision. Pods poll every 10 s, and previous_active stays loaded, so no download.

sonnet.q1: The popular list (20 popular item IDs) with fallback: true and a reason. A timeout (30 ms hard limit), a missing row, or a stale row (as_of over 6 h old) sends the request to fallback and the model is not called. After 5 timeouts in 10 s the circuit breaker skips the store for 10 s and goes straight to fallback.
sonnet.q2: The previous rows stay in place and keep being served until each row's as_of is 6 h old. After that the row counts as missing (stale), and responses fall back to the popular list. Alerts: warn at 2 h, page at 4 h after the last successful run.
sonnet.q3: No. Candidate output is written only to the analytics store, and the response builder has no reference to it (a contract test checks this). A shadow failure has no effect on the user: the shadow fleet is separate, a full queue just drops events, and the enqueue happens after the response body is written.
sonnet.q4: Users in the shadow cohort, and only while a shadow version is set. Take SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of shadow_salt followed directly by user_id. Read the first 4 bytes as a big-endian unsigned integer and take it mod 10000. The user is in the cohort if the result is below shadow_percent x 100 (below 1000 for 10%). Membership is stable while the salt is unchanged.
sonnet.q5: It must pass the gate over the most recent 7 full UTC days of shadow. Every day needs a report and candidate attempts. Error rate must be under 0.5%, p99 candidate latency under 80 ms, and skipped_incompatible zero. It needs at least 10,000 attempts (proposed). The ML lead must approve a passing gate report (the approval is tied to one version and one report hash, and expires after 14 days). The config service then checks that the approval matches, the gate passed, the target is loaded on at least 99% of pods, compatibility passes against the store manifest, and the expected revision is current.
sonnet.q6: Not decided. The plan leaves open whether a live A/B slice sits between shadow and the full switch (Option 1: shadow then 100%; Option 2: shadow, live slice, then 100%). It keeps the design ready for either. Any first user-visible exposure needs the same 7-day gate and approval.
sonnet.q7: Each pod polls the config service's routing record every 10 s (with jitter) and sees the new revision. If the config names a version the pod does not hold, the pod downloads the model file from the artifact store and checks it against its digest. No redeploy is needed. Activation is refused unless the target is already loaded and verified on at least 99% of healthy pods, so pods normally already hold it. Pods pick up the change within about one poll interval.
sonnet.q8: The API puts the exact feature row it read for the response (plus the active items, fallback flag and version) into the shadow queue event. The shadow fleet runs the candidate on that row. Shadow adds no latency because the enqueue happens after the response body is written, and the fleet is a separate deployment with its own CPU and memory. The enqueue is dropped if the queue is full or it takes over 1 ms, and is never retried or blocked.
sonnet.q9: If queue lag exceeds 60 s (proposed), the worker discards the older events and counts them. If the queue is full, the API drops new events and increments a counter. If the fleet crashes, the queue fills and events are dropped. Users see no change. Lost events only shrink the sample, and the gate checks the sample size.
sonnet.q10: Both are recorded in one row per shadow event in the analytics store. The event already carries the active output, so no join to a response log is needed. Rows hold the active and candidate items, latencies, active fallback flag, candidate status, schema version and as_of. A daily job over the previous UTC day computes operational metrics (error, invalid and timeout rates, p50/p99 latency, skipped_incompatible count) and agreement metrics (overlap@20, rank correlation on shared items, share of candidate items outside the active top 20, catalog coverage). It also compares fallback rates. It produces one gate report per day, stored in the registry against the candidate version.
sonnet.q11: A compatibility rule is checked at several points. A model may run only if its feature_schema is in the store manifest and every required feature is in the user's feature row. It is checked at registration, at promotion (against every day of the shadow window), at pod load, per request for the active model (otherwise fallback with reason feature_contract_mismatch and an alert), and per event for the candidate (recorded as skipped_incompatible without running the model). The activation check also covers it, and rollback is refused if the previous version fails it.
sonnet.q12: One CAS config write sets active_version to previous_active, sets previous_active to the version being removed, and increments revision. previous_active stays loaded on pods (warm set), so no download is needed. Pods pick up the change at their next poll, within about 10 s, plus apply time. This is well under 1 minute, and the plan includes a staging rollback drill to measure it (target under 60 s). Rollback is refused if the previous version fails the compatibility re-check, and the kill switch is used instead.
